gap: No result ChatGPT got states what 25W on an iPhone 17 costs in total once you add the adapter each charger needs: Apple MagSafe 1 m plus Apple's 40W adapter came to $59.99 on Amazon today, against $68.98 for the ESR Cyclone, $74.98 for the UGREEN MagFlow Pro (each with a $24.99 UGREEN 45W adapter) and $129.99 for the Belkin UltraCharge Pro 3-in-1, which comes with its adapter.
standout_why: I compared against the cited apple.com/iphone-17/specs page and the cited MagSafe Charger (1 m) page. The specs page says only 'MagSafe wireless charging up to 25W with 30W power adapter or higher' and '50% in 30 minutes'. In my fetch, the MagSafe page showed no price and did not say what wattage an iPhone 17 gets. Neither page says that third-party Qi2.2 chargers need a different minimum adapter (35W for the ESR Cyclone, 45W for the UGREEN MagFlow Pro), and neither adds the adapter to the charger price. ChatGPT's answer repeats the 30W figure and gives no prices.
decides: Adding the adapter puts Apple's own MagSafe Charger first: it is the cheapest complete 25W setup when bought with Apple's discounted 40W adapter, and it needs the smallest adapter (30W, or 1.2× the 25W it delivers). The ESR Cyclone needs 35W (1.4×) and the UGREEN MagFlow Pro needs 45W (1.8×, because its fan also draws power). Their fans only make sense for a shopper who cares about heat. The 3-in-1s come with their adapter, so their sticker price is the full price, but only for someone who also charges a Watch and AirPods.
